description: The §3.4 rule 1 collection cap is CUMULATIVE across the blocks of one array or map, isolated here: both blocks are individually valid (under the cap, progress-making boolean elements), so only a running-total check rejects the payload. A decoder with a per-block cap and the zero-progress rule but no cumulative counter ACCEPTS this input and fails the vector. The inputHex is honestly large (two blocks of 524300 one-byte booleans, ~1 MB of payload, ~2.1 MB of hex): the cap is 2^20 items, so no small input can exercise the cumulative path without zero-size elements. The writer side has no compact vector either — a value above the cap must list every element in the vector file — and is pinned by the symmetric encode-side checks in persona-core-lib unit tests instead.

vectors.description: Two blocks of 524300 booleans each: 524300 + 524300 = 1048600 > 2^20 cumulative items. Neither block alone exceeds the cap and every element consumes a byte, so only the cumulative counter rejects this.
